result.title: Critical Mass: Structure-Disjoint Splits Drift With the Libraries They Are Built On
result.comment: Accepted at 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026). Workshop: AI Data Readiness for Scientific Discovery
result.summary: Molecular machine learning evaluates out-of-distribution performance with structure disjoint splits, a construction rule fixed once at the scale its library happened to have: threshold a pairwise distance, then assign whole connected components to folds. For predicting structures from mass spectra, the field has converged on single-linkage clustering under the myopic Maximum Common Edge Subgraph (MCES) distance at a threshold of 10. This convention was set on 29,000 molecules but public libraries now hold 227,690 molecules. MCES is NP-hard per pair over a quadratically growing set, and so the criterion has never been evaluated at that scale. We propose an optimized version of this criterion, allowing for computationally feasible application on the public libraries: Admissible bounds and a union-find skip reduce $2.6 \times 10^{10}$ molecular pairs to only $1.15 \times 10^{7}$ integer programs, a $2{,}259\times$ saving, while provably producing the lossless partition. We find that at this scale the graph percolates. A single component holds $95.5\%$ of the library, capping any test set at $4.5\%$. What remains is not merely smaller, but systematically different: a held-out compound outweighs a training compound 88.1\% of the time, because a fixed absolute budget is a tighter relative tolerance on a larger molecule. Large library benchmarks using this splitting rule naively therefore conflate structural novelty with extrapolation to larger, more complex chemistry.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对分子机器学习中按 MCES 距离阈值做「结构不相交」OOD 划分的惯例，提出可扩展的优化实现（可容许界与并查集跳跃，将 2.6×10^10 分子对降到 1.15×10^7 次整数规划），发现在 22.7 万分子规模下图发生渗流，单一连通分量占 95.5%，且测试集系统性偏向更大的分子。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「固定绝对阈值在库规模增长后导致划分与评测指标系统性漂移」的现象，可能对 LVR 基准中按相似度构造的划分、渗流式泄漏与长度泛化评测设计提供跨域类比线索，但仅为待核查的推测，需判断是否真有方法可迁移。
